questions.question:
With reference to the Directive Principles of State policy contained in the Constitution of India, which of the following statements is/are correct?

1.Article 37 of the Constitution of India provides that the Directive Principles of State Policy are enforceable in the High Courts only.

2.Article 38 provides that the State shall strive to minimise the inequalities in income amongst individuals and groups of people.

3.Article 39 provides that the State shall direct its policy towards securing that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
questions.solution: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Article 38 directs the State to minimize inequalities in income, status, and opportunities. Article 39(d) ensures equal pay for equal work for both men and women. Correction: Statement 1 is false because Article 37 explicitly states that Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court, though they are fundamental in governance.

questions.question: Article 15 of the Constitution of India entails:
questions.option_2: prohibition of discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
questions.option_4: equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment
questions.solution: Article 15 prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. This article ensures equal access to public places like shops, restaurants, and wells. Note: It allows for special provisions for women, children, and socially/educationally backward classes.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution: Articles 12 to 35 in Part III of the Indian Constitution deal with Fundamental Rights. These rights are categorized into six broad groups: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

questions.question: Fundamental duties were introduced in Part IVA of the Constitution by the:
questions.solution: Fundamental Duties were introduced in Part IVA (Article 51A) by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. This was done based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee during the national emergency. Initially, ten duties were added.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts led to the insertion of Article 21 A?
questions.solution: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 led to the insertion of Article 21A, making Right to Education a Fundamental Right. It mandates free and compulsory education for all children between 6 and 14 years. This amendment also changed Article 45 (DPSP) and added the 11th Fundamental Duty.

questions.question: ‘Reservation in promotion’ comes under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.solution: Article 16 (4A) deals with 'Reservation in promotion'. It was inserted by the 77th Amendment Act, 1995, to enable the State to provide reservation in matters of promotion to any class or classes of posts in the services under the State in favor of the SCs and STs.

questions.question: Suppose a mine worker asks his son, aged 9 years, to help him in his work instead of going to school. Which Article of the Constitution of India will be violated in this case?
questions.solution: Article 24 will be violated. It prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment. This is a absolute right meant to protect children from exploitation and ensure their right to a healthy childhood and education.

questions.question: Articles 344 (1) and 351 of the Constitution of India are related to the:
questions.solution: Articles 344 (1) and 351 are related to the Eighth Schedule, which lists the official languages of India. Article 344(1) provides for a Commission by the President on official languages, and Article 351 provides a directive for the development and promotion of the Hindi language.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India vests plenary powers in Parliament to legislate on the subject of citizenship?
questions.solution: Article 11 vests plenary powers in Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law. Since the Constitution only provided for citizenship at its commencement (Articles 5-10), Article 11 gives Parliament the authority to make any provision for the acquisition and termination of citizenship.

questions.question: In which part of the Constitution will you find the six broad categories of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution: The six broad categories of Fundamental Rights are found in Part III of the Constitution. This part is often called the 'Magna Carta' of the Indian Constitution as it contains a long and comprehensive list of justiciable fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution is described as the ‘Magna Carta of India’?
questions.solution: Part III is described as the ‘Magna Carta of India’. This term refers to the historic charter of rights granted by King John of England in 1215. Like the original Magna Carta, Part III serves as the first major document protecting the liberties of the people against the arbitrary power of the State.

questions.question: Writ of Mandamus is a Fundamental Right classifiable under:
questions.option_4: the right to freedom of religion
questions.solution: The Writ of Mandamus (meaning 'We Command') is a Fundamental Right classifiable under Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32). It is an order issued by a court to a public official or body asking them to perform a duty they have failed to perform.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT vis-à-vis features of the Indian Constitution?

1) The Constitution empowers the Prime Minister to proclaim three types of emergencies.

2) A reservation policy is there to uplift the disadvantaged sections of society.

3)The Supreme Court has no power of judicial review.

4)The Constitution provides for universal adult suffrage.
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 3 are INCORRECT. (1) The President (not Prime Minister) proclaims emergencies. (3) The Supreme Court does have the power of Judicial Review under Articles 13, 32, and 226. True Facts: Reservation exists for upliftment, and India follows universal adult suffrage (voting rights for all adults).

questions.question: ___________ has called the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the ‘Soul of the Constitution’.
questions.solution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) the 'Soul of the Constitution' and its 'very heart'. He believed that a right without a remedy is meaningless, and Article 32 makes the Fundamental Rights real and enforceable.

questions.question: Certiorari comes under the:
questions.solution: Certiorari is one of the five writs available under the Right to Constitutional Remedies. It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to quash its order on the grounds of excess of jurisdiction or error of law.

questions.question: Indian Constitution came into force on __________ and is celebrated as Republic Day.
questions.solution: The Indian Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen specifically to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930. The adoption occurred earlier, on 26 November 1949.

questions.question: The establishment of Union Public Service Commission, State Public Service Commissions and Joint Public Service Commission falls under which of the following features of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: The establishment of Public Service Commissions is a feature of Federalism in India. It ensures that both the Union and the States have independent, merit-based recruiting bodies to maintain the integrity of the civil services at different levels of government.

questions.question: Secularism is a feature of the Indian Constitution, which means:
questions.option_1: The State promotes the religion of the majority community.
questions.option_2: The State does not promote any religion.
questions.option_3: The State can promote any religion.
questions.option_4: The State promotes the religion of the minority community.
questions.solution: In the Indian context, Secularism means that the State does not promote any religion as a state religion and maintains a 'principled distance' from all religions. It treats all religions equally and protects the freedom of all individuals to practice their faith.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act come into force?
questions.solution: The 100th Amendment Act came into force in 2015. It ratified the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh, involving the exchange of enclaves and the transition of territory to streamline the international border.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties were recommended to be inserted in the Indian Constitution by the Swarna Singh Committee?
questions.solution: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended 8 Fundamental Duties. However, the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, actually included 10 duties. Later, the 86th Amendment Act of 2002 added an 11th duty.

questions.question: Federalism in the Indian constitutional context means:
questions.option_1: the existence of more than one level of government in the country
questions.option_2: the existence only one level of government in the country
questions.option_3: the existence of states in the country
questions.option_4: the existence of one nation one government in the country
questions.solution: Federalism refers to the existence of more than one level of government in the country. In India, this includes the Central (Union) government, State governments, and the third tier consisting of Panchayats and Municipalities, each with its own sphere of authority defined by the Constitution.
